subject: Post-demo: BrightLayer integration — capacity & auth clarifications
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: BrightLayer integration — capacity & auth clarifications

Hi Samir / Lindsay,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation.  I wanted to summarize the technical items we captured and list the follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity and prepare a draft SOW.

Call highlights (technical):
- Primary workload: customer-facing chat + short-form generation (templates) plus a nightly rerank/embedding job for personalization.
- Auth & networking: BrightLayer prefers VPC peering and KMS for key management; raised interest in mTLS for service-to-service auth.
- Tooling: plan to use structured output + tool-calling for order lookup (external API) — expect calls from generated outputs.
- Expected latency SLO for generative traffic: p50 ~200-300ms, p95 ideally <700ms.

Concrete asks from our side:
1) Typical QPS (concurrent requests) and burst patterns (peak 15 min windows).
2) Average and 95th token length for prompts and completions (tokens/request).
3) Percent of requests that will use embeddings / reranking vs gen with tool-calls.
4) Any blacklisted regions or special compliance constraints.

I've attached a lightweight capacity template (cap-plan-template.xlsx) to capture the fields above — can you fill the highlighted tabs and return? That will let Karthik and the infra team produce a Dedicated sizing and autoscaling proposal.

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive with Karthik and our infra lead this week.  Do you have availability Thu or Fri (we're PST)?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cap-plan-template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightlayer.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightLayer integration — capacity & auth clarifications

Evelyn — thanks for the recap and the template.  Quick answers to start (we'll fill the sheet this afternoon):

- Typical traffic: steady-state 60 QPS, peak 250 QPS (peaks ~10–20 mins, 2–3x/day during marketing pushes).
- Avg tokens per gen request: prompt 120 tokens, completion 220 tokens; 95th percentile completion up to 900 tokens (long reports).
- Embeddings: about 35% of requests are embeddings for search/retrieval; rerank jobs run nightly across user cohorts (batch).
- Tool-calls/structured output: roughly 15% of gen requests trigger a single external API call via tool-calling.
- Compliance: must be in-us only; we require KMS-backed encryption and audit logs. VPC peering preferred.

Attaching a quick export of our recent traffic profile and a network diagram.
Attachments: brightlayer-usage.csv, network-topology.png

Happy to do Thu 16:00 PST for the technical deep-dive.

— Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightLayer

Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightLayer integration — capacity & auth clarifications

Thanks Samir — useful numbers.

A few notes from an infra/serving perspective and clarifying questions so we can produce a concrete autoscale & queueing design:

Initial sizing assumptions (rough):
- For gen traffic (avg 60 QPS, peak 250 QPS) with average completion 220 tokens, we should consider a pool with low-latency instances sized for p95 <700ms. We'll propose a dedicated low-latency pool with strict concurrency limits per GPU to avoid tail latency due to KV cache thrash.
- For embeddings and nightly rerank: separate batch pool optimized for throughput (larger batch sizes, quantized models). This can be scheduled; not latency-sensitive.

Questions / clarifications:
1) Of the peak 250 QPS, how much is expected to be synchronous chat vs background API calls? (i.e., percent requiring <700ms response budget)
2) For tool-calls: when a gen request triggers an external API call, does BrightLayer expect the overall API call to block until the external API returns (synchronous), or do you prefer an async callback pattern? Synchronous increases latency budget requirements.
3) Are there specific models you plan to use (open models or want us to suggest managed variants)? Model size affects per-GPU concurrency.

Suggested autoscale policy prototype:
- Base pool to cover 1.2x steady-state (60 QPS * 1.2 ~72 QPS capacity)
- Scaling step to add bursts in 2x increments up to provision for 250 QPS peak
- Separate queue with priority: real-time (priority 0) vs background (priority 1) with enforced concurrency thresholds.

I'll draft a capacity estimate once we have answers to (1)-(3). If Thu 16:00 PST works, I can join the call and bring a draft capacity_estimate.xlsx.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Lindsay Cho <lindsay@brightlayer.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightLayer integration — capacity & auth clarifications

Karthik — quick clarifications:

- Synchronous vs async: we prefer synchronous end-to-end for the majority of calls (customer-facing flows). Tool-calls are expected to be blocking in >85% of cases; acceptable UX requires the external API response before rendering.
- Peak composition: roughly 70% of peak QPS is customer-facing synchronous gen/chat; 30% is background or webhook-driven activity.
- Tool-call complexity: usually a single REST lookup, low payloads.
- Embeddings: 35% of requests are embeddings (search/training vectors); nightly rerank jobs cover ~200k queries and can be scheduled into off-peak windows.
- Compliance: confirm US-only. We will need KMS + audit log exports and the ability to review runtime access logs every month.

We'll fill the attached cap-plan-template and send back by EOD. Thu 16:00 PST works — please send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Lindsay
VP Engineering
BrightLayer
